Then contrast with the same block on a rough floor with μ_k = 0.10, g = 10 m/s², which does slow down.

questions.question: A ball of mass 0.2 kg rests on a vertical post of height 5 m. A bullet of mass 0.01 kg travelling horizontally with speed V hits the centre of the ball. After the collision the ball and bullet travel independently. The ball hits the ground 20 m from the foot of the post and the bullet 100 m from the foot. Take g = 10 m/s². Find V. Options: 250 m/s, 250√2 m/s, 400 m/s, 500 m/s. Use horizontal momentum and the time of fall from 5 m.
A batsman hits back a ball of mass 0.4 kg straight toward the bowler without changing its initial speed of 15 m/s. Find the impulse on the ball. Take the incoming velocity as −15 m/s.
A spherical body of mass 100 g is dropped from 10 m and rebounds to 5 m. Take g = 9.8 m/s². Find the impulse of the force imparted by the ground.

A block of mass 0.18 kg is attached to a spring of force constant 2 N/m. The coefficient of friction with the floor is 0.1. Initially the block is at rest and the spring is unstretched. An impulse is given to the block; it slides 0.06 m and comes to rest for the first time. The initial speed is V = N/10 m/s. Find N. Take g = 10 m/s².
A 50 kg person stands on ice and pushes a 10 kg box so that the box leaves at 2.0 m/s relative to the ice. Find the person’s recoil speed, and name the pair of forces that makes the recoils opposite.

questions.question: Two blocks of masses 2.0 kg and 3.0 kg, initially at rest on ice, push apart by a compressed spring between them. The 2.0 kg block moves at 3.0 m/s. Find the speed of the 3.0 kg block. External horizontal force is zero.
questions.notes: no bank item; authored. Only third-law hit is an EM/field-momentum statement, not mechanical action–reaction.

questions.question: A 60 kg skater at rest on ice pushes a 40 kg skater, who then moves at 3.0 m/s. Find the first skater’s recoil. Identify the action–reaction pair, and explain why the ice’s external force does not cancel the recoils (the ice is smooth horizontally).
questions.notes: no bank item; authored. Only third-law hit is an EM/field-momentum statement, not mechanical action–reaction.

questions.question: If the resultant of all external forces on a system is zero, then from an inertial frame the linear momentum of the system does not change in time. Prove this from ΣF_ext = dP/dt, and give one internal-force example (two skaters pushing) that conserves P but not kinetic energy.
A 0.50 kg wad of clay at 8.0 m/s embeds in a 1.5 kg block at rest on a smooth table. Find the common speed. Then say why you may use momentum conservation even though kinetic energy is lost.

questions.question: A uniform chain of length 6 m is placed on a table with part hanging over the edge. The system is at rest. The coefficient of static friction between chain and table is 0.5. Find the maximum length hanging from the table, in metres.

Two blocks m = 2 kg and M = 8 kg sit on a smooth table with m on top of M. The coefficient of static friction between the blocks is 0.5. Find the maximum horizontal force F that can be applied to M so that the blocks move together. Take g = 9.8 m/s². Options: 9.8 N, 39.2 N, 49 N, 78.4 N. The table is smooth; this is not an incline.

A ladder of mass m leans against a wall in static equilibrium at angle θ to the horizontal floor. The coefficient of friction between wall and ladder is μ1 and between floor and ladder is μ2. The normal reaction of the wall is N1 and of the floor is N2. If the ladder is about to slip, which of the following is/are true? (A) μ1 = 0, μ2 ≠ 0 and N2 tanθ = mg/2 (B) μ1 ≠ 0, μ2 = 0 and N1 tanθ = mg/2 (C) μ1 ≠ 0, μ2 ≠ 0 and N2 = mg / (1 + μ1 μ2) (D) μ1 = 0, μ2 ≠ 0 and N1 tanθ = mg/2.
Define rolling friction (rolling resistance) and contrast it with kinetic friction of sliding. Why is the rolling-friction force usually much smaller than μ_k N for the same surfaces?

questions.question: A cylinder of weight 100 N rolls at constant speed on the level under a horizontal pull of 2.0 N applied at the axle. Find the rolling-friction force and say where it acts. This is not rolling without slipping on an incline (Unit 5).

questions.question: A cubic block of mass m slides down a 60° incline with acceleration g/2. Take g as given. Find the coefficient of kinetic friction. Options included (√3 − 1), 1/2, 1/√3. Use a = g(sinθ − μ cosθ).

The time taken by a block of mass m to slide down from the highest point to the lowest point on a rough 45° incline is 50% more than on an identical smooth 45° incline. Find the coefficient of kinetic friction. Options: 3/4, 2/3, 5/9, 4/9.
A block moves on a 45° incline with coefficient of friction μ. The force required to just push it up the plane is 3 times the force required to just prevent it from sliding down. If N = 10μ, find N.
A light string over a smooth light fixed pulley connects two blocks. If the acceleration of the system is g/8, find the ratio of the masses (larger/smaller). Options included 9/7, 8/7, 9/8, 7/5.
A light string over a smooth light pulley connects masses m1 and m2 (m2 > m1). If the acceleration is g/√2, find m2/m1. Options included (√2+1)/(√2−1) and (1+√5)/(√5−1).

A light inextensible string over a smooth fixed pulley connects masses 0.36 kg and 0.72 kg. Take g = 10 m/s². Find the work done (in joules) by the string on the 0.36 kg block during the first second after release from rest.

A person standing in an elevator experiences weight loss in which situation? (A) elevator moves upward with constant acceleration (B) elevator moves downward with constant acceleration (C) elevator moves upward with uniform velocity (D) elevator moves downward with uniform velocity.

A person in a lift holds a water jar with a small hole at the lower end of its side. When the lift is at rest, the water jet hits the lift floor 1.2 m from the person. Match each motion with the landing distance d of the jet on the lift floor: (P) lift accelerating vertically up (Q) lift accelerating vertically down with a < g (R) lift moving vertically up at constant speed (S) lift in free fall; (1) d = 1.2 m (2) d > 1.2 m (3) d < 1.2 m (4) no water leaks out.

A person in an elevator performs a weighing experiment with a 50 kg object. The height of the elevator from the ground is y = 8 [1 + sin(2π t / T)] metres with T = 40π s. Take g = 10 m/s². Find the maximum variation of the object’s weight (in N) as observed in the experiment.

If the radii of curvature of the paths of two particles of the same mass are in the ratio 3 : 4, then in order to have the same centripetal force their speeds are in the ratio: (A) √3 : 1 (B) 1 : √3 (C) √3 : 2 (D) 2 : √3. Use F = m v² / r.
